sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Caen is cutting road space for a tram while loosening its on-street charges. The city's page, updated on 25 September 2026, shows paid parking Monday to Saturday from 9:30 to 12:30 and 14:00 to 19:00: 1.80 euros an hour in the red city-core zone with a 2h30 maximum, 1.30 euros in the yellow zone with 5h30, and a free green zone [0]. The post-parking charge is 33 euros [1]. Residents of the centre can buy a permit at 15 euros a month or 150 a year for a first vehicle and 500 a year for a second [2]. From 2 November 2026 the city will give one free hour on Wednesdays and two on Saturdays on surface parking in the red and yellow zones, excluding some barrier car parks [3]. ICI reported that the free hours are planned to last until the end of the tram works, at an estimated cost of 700,000 to 900,000 euros against nearly 5 million euros of total parking revenue [4]. The city's offers also include 30 free minutes in two underground car parks and a 1.50-euro night rate [6].

The low-emission zone has applied since 1 January 2025 inside the ring road and bars only unclassified vehicles, about 2,000 counted; its page mentions a tolerance period [8]. The Constitutional Council struck down the clause that would have abolished such zones on 21 May 2026 [9]. In the March 2026 election campaign the outgoing mayor proposed a new car park of 350 to 400 spaces next to the centre; it is a campaign proposal and we found no confirmation [16].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The tram extension drives the change. Caen la mer's FAQ says the works run from April 2026 to the end of 2028, with service planned for summer 2029, over 9.1 km with 17 new stations and a cost of 288.5 million euros excluding tax at 2021 values [10]. Main boulevards were cut to one lane each way from spring 2026, and rue de Bernières is to close to through traffic from the first quarter of 2027 [11]. On-street spaces will be removed temporarily as works advance, while the Doumer, République, Hôtel de Ville and Gardin underground car parks stay open and the number and location of spaces will change permanently after the redesign [12]. The Pompidou park-and-ride became accessible on 6 July 2026 after nine months of works, with 235 park-and-ride spaces [13]. Twisto lists three park-and-rides, Côte de Nacre (149 spaces), Ifs Jean Vilar (79) and Pompidou (249), and two proximity car parks of 90 spaces each [14]. The city says 22 charging stations are installed [17].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Indigo holds the delegation for the central underground car parks and, according to Tendance Ouest, has invested 3.7 million euros in them since the start of 2025; the paper names six, which in theory offer 2,015 spaces, and reports that the Caen la mer president said the Résistance car park is below 50% occupancy in its evening peak [5]. The Hôtel de Ville car park is managed by Indigo, open 24 hours with live availability on Indigo's app [7]. RATP Dev has run the Twisto network since 1 January 2025 under a six-year contract and was to be tasked with managing the park-and-rides [15].

Our data cover only one car park, the Côte de Nacre park-and-ride, with 145 spaces in the feed, measured since 5 October 2026. Occupancy averaged about 22% on weekdays and 19% at weekends, and never exceeded 41%. We have no live data for the central Indigo car parks, so we cannot test the statement about low occupancy, and the figures are about two and a half weeks.
